source.title: Pre-interpolation loss behaviour in neural networks
source.citation: Arthur E. W. Venter et al., 2021
source.authors: Arthur E. W. Venter; Marthinus W. Theunissen; Marelie Hattingh Davel

record.tranche_reason: The study measures validation accuracy and loss during training, which bears on epoch-wise error behaviour, but it does not run a full double-descent experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper varies network widths, training-set sizes and other settings, but does not report a test-error-versus-model-size curve or test error as training-set size changes near interpolation. Its comparisons of validation metrics at minimum validation loss and at interpolation are not full epoch-wise fall-rise-fall curves. Double descent results cited from other work are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study examines why average validation loss rises while validation accuracy stays stable or improves in MLP classifiers. It mentions double descent only as background. It does not measure test error as a function of model size, epochs or sample count to look for a fall-rise-fall shape. Its sweep comparisons use two points per model: the epoch of minimum validation loss and first interpolation or the final epoch. Models A-D were chosen because they show the loss/accuracy divergence. So no version of the claim is tested by the study's own results.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that, with large enough capacity, validation loss and accuracy can both increase during training. The loss rise comes from a minority of specific validation samples with progressively extreme losses, linked to growing weight magnitudes. They caution that average validation loss is a poor overfitting estimate and that loss and accuracy should not be assumed negatively correlated.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies validation loss and accuracy, per-sample losses, and weight distributions in MLP classifiers; it does not reproduce a double-descent capacity or sample-size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported loss/accuracy behaviour varies with model capacity, dataset difficulty, and training-set size; FMNIST and smaller training sets show larger increases in validation loss while accuracy improves.

fits_no_version.finding: In MLPs on MNIST/FMNIST, average validation loss rises after an early minimum while validation accuracy is stable or improves. The rise is driven by a small, persistent minority of validation samples with growing extreme losses, coinciding with growth in some weight magnitudes. The effect is more frequent for larger models, smaller training sets and FMNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Held-out average cross-entropy loss can increase during training while accuracy holds or improves, because a few samples acquire extreme losses; loss and accuracy need not be inversely related.

record.problems: The study describes a small, selected set of models for its per-sample analyses; many results are qualitative or presented in plots, with no uncertainty estimates. Its measurements are validation metrics and do not establish full double-descent curves.
record.rows_left_out: No additional per-model numerical rows were available in the text: the reported sweep comparisons are qualitative summaries, and the plot values are not stated numerically.

untested.parts: Hidden width is varied in Sec 4.1, but no test-error-vs-width curve or interpolation-threshold peak is reported.
No epoch-wise test-error curve is analysed for a fall-rise-fall shape.
No sample-size sweep near interpolation is reported.
There is no label-noise or regularization manipulation; regularizers were deliberately omitted.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Nakkiran et al. (1912.02292) and Belkin et al. (1812.11118) only in the background section. The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V2 labels are withdrawn: the measured construct, loss/accuracy divergence, is related to but different from double descent.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error curve across model sizes or peak near the interpolation threshold.
The study reports validation accuracy and loss at selected training points and for selected learning curves, not a systematic full fall-rise-fall test-error curve over epochs.
Training-set sizes vary, but the study does not measure whether increasing sample size raises test error near interpolation.
No comparison of double descent across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak locations.
No test of label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameter number.

rows.subject: Two-layer MLPs (95 models, reported as a group)
rows.size_stated: Hidden-layer width ranged from 7 to 2,000 nodes
rows.operation_detail: Compared validation metrics at minimum validation loss and first training-set interpolation

conditions.value: Adam for 57 models; SGD for 38 models

rows.baseline: At the epoch with minimum validation loss
rows.value: At first interpolation, limited-capacity models had decreasing validation accuracy; larger models tended to show increasing validation accuracy and validation loss before interpolation.
rows.note: Group-level qualitative description; the paper does not give per-model accuracy values in the text or a complete epoch-wise curve.
rows.check: The row compares validation accuracy at minimum validation loss with accuracy at first interpolation. Two points cannot show an epoch-wise fall-rise-fall curve, and the study does not frame the result as double descent. Small models losing accuracy and large models gaining it bears on the loss/accuracy divergence, not on V2.

rows.subject: MLPs with varying hyperparameters (80 models, reported as a group)
rows.size_stated: 1, 3, or 10 hidden layers; 100 or 1,000 nodes per layer
rows.operation_detail: Compared validation metrics at minimum validation loss and the end of training or maximum training accuracy

conditions.value: varied as defined in Figure 3 legend

rows.baseline: At the epoch with minimum validation loss
rows.value: FMNIST models tended to show larger validation-loss increases while validation accuracy was still improving than MNIST models; models trained on MNIST or larger training sets generally had higher validation accuracy.
rows.note: The reported comparison is qualitative and does not establish a complete epoch-wise error curve.
rows.check: This is a two-point comparison across a hyperparameter sweep of 80 models, with no epoch-wise error curve. The observation that larger training sets and MNIST give higher accuracy is a general performance description, not a double-descent test.

rows.subject: Selected models A-D (reported together)
rows.operation_detail: Observed validation learning curves during training

conditions.value: A: 5,000 MNIST, Adam, batch 64; B: 5,000 MNIST, SGD, batch 64; C: 5,000 FMNIST, SGD, batch 64; D: 55,000 FMNIST, Adam, batch 16

rows.value: For all four models, validation accuracy was stable or improving slightly beyond the early minimum in validation loss.
rows.note: The paper reports the selected models together; it does not assign the stable-versus-improving description separately to each model. Stable or improving accuracy corresponds to no reported rise in classification error over this interval.
rows.check: Models A-D were selected because they show the loss/accuracy divergence, so this is a selection-dependent case study. Stable or improving accuracy after the loss minimum does not test a fall-rise-fall error curve, which the authors never examine. The state 'reversed' is unsupported.

rows.subject: Selected models A-D (loss distributions reported as a group)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked per-sample loss distributions during training

conditions.value: A-D; A shown in Figure 5 and B-D in Appendix Figure 8

rows.baseline: Earlier training iterations, not stated numerically
rows.value: Loss decreased for a vast majority of samples; a small minority of validation and evaluation samples had increasing loss values.
rows.note: This is a finding about sample-level loss behaviour, not a measured double-descent curve.

rows.subject: Selected models A-D (outlier analysis reported as a group)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked how often validation samples exceeded the upper Tukey fence
rows.value: Validation samples with extreme end-of-training loss were usually outliers for most of training; a large majority were never outliers and had small final loss.
rows.note: The text gives the result for the four selected models collectively.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported validation-accuracy direction varies with capacity and dataset, and the comparisons do not show a complete fall-rise-fall error curve (r1, r2).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Selected models A-D, after the early minimum in validation loss
reader_labels.reason: For these models, validation accuracy is described as stable or improving, rather than falling as expected during an intermediate rise in classification error (r3).
